html:
In three days in May 1944 the Soviet secret police deported the whole Crimean Tatar people, at least 191,000 people, from Crimea to Central Asia, mostly to Uzbekistan. Crimean Tatars call it the Sürgünlik, the exile.

The Crimean Tatars were the native Muslim people of Crimea, once the core of the Crimean Khanate. When the Red Army retook Crimea from Nazi Germany, Stalin accused the whole people of collaboration. Lavrentiy Beria ran the operation, and the NKVD loaded families, even Red Army soldiers and Communist Party members, onto cattle trains.

Many died on the journey and many more in the first years, from hunger and disease, in the special settlements where they were held. They were not allowed to go home until 1989; since then many have returned. The deportation is shown on the chart in Europe too, as the Crimean Tatar deportation, and followed the deportation of the Koreans seven years earlier.
